title.narrative: Promoting Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy production in the Community-Based Tourism Sector in Central Asia

description.narrative: The overall objective of the proposed intervention is to contribute to the reduction of the carbon footprint in Community-Based Tourism Industry in Central Asia, in particular in Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan. This will be achieved by realising the following two outcomes: 1) Micro Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the renewable energy (RE), energy efficiency (EE) and community-based tourism (CBT) sectors are supported to adopt Sustainable Consumption Practices (SCP) practices and get access to finance; and 2) an enabling environment to strengthen SCP in the RE, EE and CBT sectors in Central Asia is created.

And subsequently the percentage of respondents who agreed or answered affirmatively was calculated for the final value.

comment.narrative: For the baseline assessment conducted in SeptemberOctober 2020 a quantitative approach was adopted. Closedended questionnaires were utilized for data collection aiming to quantify indicators and generalize results. Data entry occurred directly into the KoBo Toolbox during beneficiary interviews to mitigate errors. Random sampling was employed to ensure statistical validity focusing on 315 CBT MSMEs under the SWITCH II Project. Initially a sample size of 174 respondents was calculated with a 95 confidence level and a 5 margin of error. However the survey ultimately reached 225 CBT MSMEs across three countries 73 in Kyrgyzstan 73 in Uzbekistan and 79 in Tajikistan.During the baseline assessment a quantitative approach was adopted utilizing questionnaires with closedended questions for extensive data collection enabling generalization to broader target groups. Data were collected electronically using the KoBo Toolbox to minimize errors followed by thorough data cleaning to rectify any inaccuracies. Additionally followup calls were made to clarify incomplete information. The reviewed data underwent assessment by the Monitoring and Evaluation team before final validation by project management.
From baseline

For the endline external evaluation the same approach was utilized as for the baseline related to tools and convenience sampling was used. With this the target sample size for CBT MSMEs was 249 respondents 83 per country. However ultimately only 208 CBT MSMEs were reached 85 in Kyrgyzstan 48 in Tajikistan and 75 in Uzbekistan.The endline external evaluation methodology involved a quantitative survey with closedended questionnaires with yes and no answers adapted from the baseline ones. The percentage of respondents who answered affirmatively was calculated for the final result. Data were collected using Computer Assisted Telephone Interviewing CATI with operators conducting interviews over the phone. The Kobo Toolbox application was utilized to program the questionnaire and data collection took place in JuneJuly 2023.

comment.narrative: Within the baseline assessment which took place in SeptemberOctober 2020 random sampling was employed with a target of 130 REEE MSMEs. This resulted in a sample size of 98 REEE respondents however ultimately only 63 MSMEs were surveyed 20 in Uzbekistan 21 in Kyrgyzstan and 22 in Tajikistan. Employing a quantitative approach closedended questionnaires were used for data collection facilitated by KoBo Toolbox to minimize errors. Data cleaning rectified incorrect or missing values postcollection
30 of increase from the baseline value should be achieved for three countries Tajikistan from 5 to 35 for Uzbekistan from 25 to 55 and for Kyrgyzstan from 42 to 72

For the endline external evaluation similar quantitative surveys were conducted targeting 98 REEE MSMEs across the three countries utilizing a convenience sampling approach . Data collection occurred via Computer Assisted Telephone Interviewing CATI between June 15 and July 3 2023 involving 3 operators in Kyrgyzstan 3 in Uzbekistan and 5 in Tajikistan. The final sample included 97 REEE MSMEs 27 in Kyrgyzstan 32 in Tajikistan and 38 in Uzbekistan.For this indicator the survey question inquired about how EERE MSMEs perceive the level of representation of their interests at both local and national levels. Respondents who rated the representation as satisfactory or better were included in the final tally.

description.narrative: of bylaws drafted on improving the regulatory framework for RE/EE production

comment.narrative: A business environment analysis was conducted in each country leading to the establishment of working groups in Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan for advocacy recommendations. Additionally focus group discussions FGDs and consultations with key stakeholders were held including ministries MSMEs CSOs business associations and legal consultants.During project implementation Intersectoral Working Groups IWG members along with expert groups and the business community developed roadmaps with recommendations to address barriers in clean energy production and consumption in tourism and microgeneration based on renewable energy sources in CBT entities. These were presented at an extended IWG meeting in June 2022. Three press releases were produced on the bylaws on improving the regulatory framework for REEE production.In the final external assessment survey it was reported that changes to the draft law on tourism based on this roadmap with recommendations were made in Kyrgyzstan and forwarded to the national Parliament. However no progress was reported in Tajikistan and Uzbekistan regarding improvements to the regulatory framework for REEE production.
